newsitem.title: USA: Police break up Beanie Baby caper in Illinois.
newsitem.headline: Police break up Beanie Baby caper in Illinois.

text.p: A 77-year-old man has been charged with stealing an estimated 1,200 Beanie Baby stuffed toys, the latest children's craze, police said on Wednesday.

The hard-to-get toys, which are all the rage among young children and their desperate parents, were allegedly stolen from a suburban Chicago warehouse owned by manufacturer Ty Inc. and were being sold at a fruit market.

Police charged Ben Perri, 77, and released him on $500 bond last weekend after being led to his home by a private investigator hired by the company. The toys come in an array of 118 animal likenesses and retail for about $5, although collectors will pay as much as $800 for retired models.
"They're very popular," company spokeswoman Anne Nickels said of the toys, noting that buyers empty store shelves as soon as new shipments arrive.
